claims.proposition_evaluated: Among separately saleable replacement dwellings on Edmonton lots where one existing dwelling was demolished for infill, more than 50 percent have a higher first arm's-length sale price than the demolished dwelling's last arm's-length sale price, in constant dollars. Count every separately saleable replacement dwelling once. Report lot-level shares under the 'every replacement' and 'at least one replacement' rules as declared sensitivities. Report alongside the verdict the median replacement-to-demolished price ratio and the distribution of that ratio.
claims.interpretation_notes: The public record does not contain a lot-to-lot joined dataset of prior arm's-length sale prices and replacement arm's-length sale prices. Without this, the 50 percent threshold cannot be tested on the required denominator.
limitations: Publicly available datasets from the City of Edmonton (Open Data) include property assessments and building/demolition permits, but do not provide historical arm's-length sale prices linked lot-by-lot.
Real estate board data on arm's-length sale prices is proprietary and not published in bulk.
unknowns: The actual arm's-length sale prices of demolished dwellings.
The actual first arm's-length sale prices of the separately saleable replacement dwellings.

missing_evidence.description: A dataset joining residential demolition permits with both the last arm's-length sale price of the demolished dwelling and the first arm's-length sale price of the replacement dwelling(s).
missing_evidence.likely_holder: REALTORS Association of Edmonton (RAE) or a municipal open-data initiative partnering with Land Titles.

calculations_needed: Match demolition permits to new building permits/completed dwellings by parcel identifier.
Retrieve last sale price before demolition and first sale price after completion.
Adjust prior sale price to constant dollars using the Edmonton CMA CPI.
Calculate the median replacement-to-demolished price ratio and the lot-level sensitivities.
what_would_change_my_verdict: Publication of a comprehensive analytical report or dataset that links demolition and replacement arm's-length sale prices lot-by-lot for Edmonton.
claims.suggested_one_line: The public record does not contain the linked sale-price data needed to test whether most infill replacements sell for more than the demolished house did.
claims.suggested_short_answer: We cannot establish if most replacement infill homes sell for more than the demolished dwellings. The required data—historical arm's-length sale prices linked lot-by-lot to new replacement sale prices—is proprietary and not available in public municipal datasets.
suggested_tldr: The claim compares the sale price of a torn-down house with the sale price of its replacements.
Testing this requires joining historical sale prices with new sale prices on the same lot.
This data is held by real estate boards and is not publicly available for bulk analysis.
Therefore, the claim cannot be tested using public evidence.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Among separately saleable replacement dwellings in the matched set, more than 50 percent would require shelter costs exceeding 30 percent of before-tax income for a hypothetical household earning the declared City median income, under the 25-year amortization and the other primary assumptions below.
claims.interpretation_notes: Because the replacement arm's-length sale prices cannot be established lot-by-lot (see Claim 1), the shelter-cost-to-income test cannot be performed for the matched set. The upper and lower bounds encompass the 50 percent threshold.
limitations: The shelter-cost calculation relies on the first arm's-length sale price of each replacement dwelling.
Without the matched set of replacement dwellings and their sale prices, the 30-percent affordability test cannot be calculated on the denominator.
unknowns: The first arm's-length sale prices of the separately saleable replacement dwellings in the matched set.

missing_evidence.description: The first arm's-length sale prices of the separately saleable replacement dwellings on lots where a demolition occurred.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: REALTORS Association of Edmonton (RAE) or Land Titles.

calculations_needed: Determine the first arm's-length sale price of each replacement dwelling.
Calculate the down payment, mortgage principal, and interest using the BoC 5-year rate and 25-year amortization.
Add property taxes, utilities, and condominium fees.
Compare total monthly shelter costs to 30 percent of the Statistics Canada median monthly before-tax household income for Edmonton.
what_would_change_my_verdict: Access to the replacement arm's-length sale prices for the matched set of demolition lots, enabling the shelter-cost calculation.
claims.suggested_one_line: The affordability of replacement infill cannot be tested without public access to their actual sale prices.
claims.suggested_short_answer: We cannot test whether most new infill homes exceed the 30-percent affordability threshold. Calculating the mortgage and shelter costs requires the actual sale prices of the new homes, which are not publicly available as a linked dataset.
suggested_tldr: The claim asserts that replacement infill housing is not affordable for a median-income household.
Testing this requires calculating the monthly shelter costs (mortgage, taxes, utilities) based on the new home's sale price.
Because the actual sale prices of the replacement homes in the matched set are not publicly available, this calculation cannot be performed.
Therefore, the affordability threshold cannot be tested on the required group of homes.
